sentences.text: Plea of accused : Pleaded not guilty.
Date of Order : 05.03.2025  3 C.C. 8418/ 2021  JUDGMENT
The complainant has filed this complaint under section 200 of the Cr.P.C., alleging that the accused has committed an offence punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

2. The brief facts of the complainant's case are as follows :
This is the case of the complainant that, he and the accused well known to each since 6 years, one of his friend by name Narasimha introduced the accused to the complainant, based on friendship the accused approached the complainant in the 2nd week of October 2019 and sought financial assistance of 7 lakhs to meet his urgent financial needs of his civil contract work .
Accordingly the complainant lent a loan of Rs.7 lakhs to the accused in the 2nd week of December 2019.
The complainant paid the amount to the accused out of the land acquisition compensation amount received by his father.
The accused undertook to repay the loan within 6 months.

After completion of the term, the complainant asked the accused to repay the loan,
accordingly the accused paid a sum of Rs.54,500/- by way of cash in July 2020, and to repay the outstanding amount, he had issued a cheque bearing No.135983 dated 30.12.2020 drawn on SBI, Akkur Branch, Channapatna Taluk for Rs.6,45,500/-.

The complainant presented the said cheque for collection through his banker i.e. Punjab National Bank, T. Dasarahalli Branch, Bangalore on 13.01.2021, but the said cheque came to be dishonoured with an endorsement "Funds insufficient" as per the cheque return memo dated 14.01.2021.
The factum of dishonour of cheque was duly communicated to the accused by issuing a legal notice dated 11.02.2021, but the notice came to be returned with an endorsement 'Addressee always absent'.

The complainant sent the legal notice to the last known address of the accused, hence it is deemed service of notice to the accused ; despite the issuance of the legal notice, the accused did not come forward to pay the cheque amount nor issue any reply notice;
hence, the complainant has filed this complaint against the accused.

3. The court, after receipt of the complaint, verified it; later, the complainant entered the witness box to depose his sworn statement in the form of an affidavit and also got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.5.

After the recording of the sworn statement, the court satisfied that the complainant made out valid grounds to take cognizance of the offence; accordingly, the court took cognizance of the offence punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, registered the criminal Chayavardhana N vs Nagaraju N on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141438702/
2 case, and also issued a summons to the accused.
On receipt of the summons, the accused appeared before this court through his counsel and got enlarged on bail.
In compliance with section 207 of the Cr.P.C., a copy of the complaint and other relevant documents were supplied to the accused.
The substance of the accusation was read over to him; he did not plead guilty and claimed to be tried.

When the case was set for complainant side evidence, the complainant moved an application under section 145(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Act with a prayer to treat the sworn statement affidavit of the complainant as his chief examination.

The court allowed the application and treated the sworn statement affidavit of the complainant as his chief examination, and the documents marked at the time of recording of his sworn statement were adopted as documentary evidence.
The learned counsel for the accused has fully cross-examined the PW.1 after the closure of the complainant's side evidence.
The statement of the accused under section 313 of the Cr.P.C. was recorded by explaining to him the incriminating evidence available in the complainant's evidence.

The accused has denied the entire evidence of the complainant and, to prove his defense, examined himself on oath as DW.1,
and got marked documents as per Ex.D.1 and D.2, despite of granting sufficient time the learned counsel for the complainant has not come forward to cross-examine DW1, consequently the cross-examination of DW1 by the complainant was taken nil.
4. On perusal of the material records placed before this court, the following points that arise for my consideration.
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the accused has successfully rebutted the presumption available against him under section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act that, he had not issued the cheques in favor of the complainant to pay the legally enforceable debt?
2. Whether the complainant has complied with the mandatory requirements of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act?
3. What order or sentence?
5. The learned counsel for the complainant has not canvased his arguments, the learned counsel for the accused has submitted that his arguments on merits may be taken as heard.
6. On careful analysis the oral and documentary evidence provided by the complainant and the accused, my answers to the above points are as follows..
Point No.1 In the negative Point No.2 In the affirmative Point No.3

As per the final order for the following REASONS Point No.1 and 2:
7.

These points are interrelated to each other, and findings given one point having a direct impact on other points; hence, to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of the evidence, both points are taken together for common discussion.

sentences.text: the complainant submits that, he lent a loan of Rs.7 lakhs to the accused to meet out his expenses of the civil contract works.

The accused borrowed the loan in the 2nd week of December 2019, out of total amount the accused had repaid Rs.54,500/- in the month of July 2020 and to repay the outstanding amount the accused had issued the disputed cheque, as per the bank endorsement the cheque in question was dishonored due to "Funds insufficient".
The legal notice returned un-served due to 'Addressee always absent'.

The accused after appearance in this case has not made any effort to give the reply notice to the complainant and also has not made any effort to show that at the time of issuance of the alleged cheque he had sufficient balance in his bank account.

The complainant has sent the legal notice to last known address of the accused, and the to prove his correct address the accused himself has produced attested copy of the aadhar card marked as Ex.D2, wherein it is disclosed that, the address mentioned by the complainant in the Ex.P.5 / legal notice and the address mentioned in Ex.D2 are one and the same.

9. The accused has not disputed the signature appeared on Ex.P1, but he disputes the issuance of cheque, according to him the cheque in question was issued in favour of one Puttaraju from whom he had borrowed a loan, the said Puttaraju and the complainant have misused the cheque and filed this present complaint, in support of his contention the accused has produced the account statement as per Ex.D1, but the there is no evidence forthcoming from the accused to prove that he had issued the cheque to one Puttaraju and he has not made any effort to issue summons to Puttaraju to depose evidence on his behalf in respect of the issuance of the cheque.
Though the learned counsel for the accused has duly cross examined the PW1 but nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth to prove that the disputed cheque was issued in favour of one Puttaraju.
Furthermore the accused has not taken any legal action against the complainant regarding misuse of cheque.

The complainant to prove his case has produced the documents at Ex.P1 to P5, among these Ex.P1 is cheque issued by the accused, wherein it is mentioned that the accused had issued the cheque in favour of the complainant to pay the legally enforceable debt, the signature of the accused was marked as Ex.P1 (a), Ex.P2 is the cheque returns memo, wherein it is mentioned that the cheque issued by the accused in favour of the complainant returned with an endorsement "Funds insufficient", Ex.P3 is the legal notice given to the accused by the complainant calling upon him to pay the cheque amount.
The said notice was sent to the last known address of the accused.
Ex.P4 is are the postal receipt

,
Ex.P5 is the postal envelop.

The accused in his 313 statement has stated that, he does not know the complainant, if it is true then the accused could have taken appropriate legal action against the complainant, but he has not taken any steps.

Further more the accused is a bank employee and he is having knowledge regarding the issuance of the cheque, and its consequences, despite of that, he kept quite without initiating the legal action against the complainant.
The accused in his chief examination has stated that, he has borrowed a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- from one Puttaswamy and issued the disputed cheque as a security.
10. The accused in his chief examination deposed that, the legal notice sent to him was not served.

In this regard I have relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in the case of C.NIRANJAN YADAV VS D.RAVIKUMAR, decided in Criminal Revision Petition No.814/2021 dated 24.06.2024, has held that, " whether the address of the accused which is known to the complainant has been properly mentioned on the registered cover.

If it is sent to such registered address, responsibility of the complainant would end and it is for the accused to say as to why he Chayavardhana N vs Nagaraju N on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141438702/
4 could not receive the cover.

sentences.text:
The presumption under the General Clauses Act,1897, would go to show that if a person has addressed a registered letter to the last known address that was known to a particular person, it is deemed to have been served."
11.
In such circumstances, where the accused admitted that the address shown in Ex.D.2 is his correct address then he cannot take the defense that the legal notice was not duly served to him.

12. As per Section 139 of the NI Act, the presumption is in favour of the complainant, that means until the accused proves that the cheque in question has not been issued to pay the legally enforceable debt, then it is to be presumed that those cheques have been issued by the accused to pay the legally enforceable debt.

13. The accused has not taken any valid defence to prove before the court that there is no payment due to the complainant, hence the complainant proves that the accused issued the cheques to pay a legally enforceable debt.
14.
The learned counsel for the accused has examined PW1 at length but no valuable information has come out of the mouth of the complainant that there is no legally enforceable debt.

15. The complainant has proved the correct address of the accused, the accused himself has produced aadhar card as per Ex.D2, the address mentioned in the aadhar card and legal notice are one and the same the accused failed to prove that he had given the cheque to one Mr. Puttaswamy,
and he has not made any effort to examine him before the court.

The cheque issued by the accused was dishonoured due to "insufficient funds", the learned counsel for complainant has not cross examined the DW1, but it is not the ground to disbelieve the case of the complainant.

The accused has to rebut the presumption with cogent evidence, The accused has not denied the signature appeared on the cheque belongs to him, once the accused admits the issuance of the cheque and the signature appeared on the cheque then the court has to presume that the accused had issued the cheque to pay the legally enforceable debt.

16. The learned counsel for the accused and complainant have not canvased their arguments, but considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that, the complainant has proved the issuance of cheque to pay the legally enforceable debt, on contrary the accused has failed to prove that the disputed cheque has been given to one Puttaswamy 17.
The accused can take any kind of defences, but those defenses must be supported by strong and admissible evidence.

18. The accused has not successfully rebutted the presumption under Section 139 of the NI Act, on the contrary the complainant has proved the initial burden regarding the existence of a legally enforceable debt.
The accused has taken a long time to pay the outstanding amount, but he has failed to pay the amount and has made the complainant wait for more than 6 years till he gets the relief from the court

, in such circumstances the court has to exercise its discretion to award adequate and sufficient relief, hence the accused is required to pay an additional compensation of Chayavardhana N vs Nagaraju N on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141438702/
5 Rs.1,00,000/- to compensate the financial loss suffered by the complainant.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is a fit case to convict the accused.
Accordingly, I answer point no.1 in the negative and point no.2 answered in the affirmative.

Point No.3 :
19.

For the above said reasons and discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Acting under section 255(2) of the Cr.P.C the accused is hereby convicted for the offense punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

The accused shall pay a fine of Rs.7,50,500/- (which includes cheque amount of Rs.6,45,500/-, additional compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- and fine amount of Rs.5,000/- payable to the government) in default accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for Six month for the offense punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act.

As per Section 357 of Cr.P.C. out of the fine amount Rs.7,45,500/-(which includes cheque amount and additional compensation amount) is to be paid to the complainant as compensation and the balance amount is to be remitted to the state government.
Bail bond and surety bond of the accused shall stand canceled.

Further, in exercise of power conferred under section 424(1)(a) of Cr.P.C the accused is permitted to pay/deposit the fine amount of Rs.7,50,500/- within 30 days from this order and execution of sentence passed against him in view of the above permission stands suspended for a period of 30 days from today.
Supply free copy of the judgment to the accused.
